author: @simplifyinai
title_or_hook: Graphify + Obsidian + Claude Code: docs → knowledge graph → vault
summary: Graphify is an open-source CLI + AI-assistant skill that turns a folder of code, docs, papers, and media into a queryable knowledge graph instead of leaving an agent to grep raw files. Three passes: (a) a deterministic tree-sitter AST pass over code (36 languages; classes, functions, imports, call graphs; no LLM, no API key); (b) local faster-whisper transcription of audio/video; (c) Claude subagents extracting concepts, relationships, and rationale from docs/papers/images/transcripts. The merged NetworkX graph is clustered with Leiden community detection (no embeddings/vector DB), and every edge carries a provenance label: EXTRACTED (from the AST), INFERRED (model-generated), or AMBIGUOUS. Outputs: graph.html, graph.json (persistent), GRAPH_REPORT.md (god nodes, surprising connections, suggested questions), and exports to Obsidian vault, Neo4j, FalkorDB, GraphML, SVG, and a markdown wiki. Installs as a skill in 17+ harnesses (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Gemini CLI, Copilot, Antigravity, Hermes, others) and exposes an MCP endpoint. The post's workflow maps 145 pages of Claude Code docs, exports the map as an Obsidian vault (graphify --obsidian), and has Claude pull source text back into each note. Free and open source; license conflict in secondary sources (Apache 2.0 vs MIT) -- verify the repo LICENSE before integration. The poster's $10K/mo claim is UNVERIFIED.
engine_training_value: Indirect: a provenance-labelled graph over the research corpus is retrieval infrastructure for the reasoning layer, not training data. The graph's own edge labels (EXTRACTED/INFERRED/AMBIGUOUS with sources) are a labelled dataset shape -- claim-provenance triples the fleet could learn verification behaviour from. No metric or label for the prediction engine itself.

author: @abcnews
title_or_hook: Starship Flight 15: booster catch aborted, Ship 42 to orbit
summary: News post on SpaceX Starship Flight 15 (Nov 13), VERIFIED this run: lifted off from Starbase at 4:47 PM CT Nov 13; ~6.5 minutes in, the automated system called off Booster 22's (first V3 Super Heavy) tower catch -- attributed on the webcast to a GNC issue the booster detected itself; the booster diverted offshore and exploded just before splashdown in the Gulf of Mexico. Ship 42 inserted into orbit at ~275 km, deployed 26 Starlink V3 satellites, and was planned to orbit ~22 hours / ~14 orbits before a first-ever upper-stage tower catch attempt on Sat Nov 14. SpaceX has not publicly established the precise abort cause.

author: @bilawal.ai
title_or_hook: "God's Eye View": a 34-second ADS-B reconstruction of the ground stop
summary: A data-visualization reconstruction of the Nov 13 FAA ground stop: a 34-second timelapse fusing public ADS-B, geostationary satellite imagery, FAA advisories, and ATC audio -- blue = aircraft airborne, orange = on the ground, rings = aircraft piling up per airport with counts. VERIFIED closing numbers this run (superseding the post's mid-event figures): the stop was issued at 3:54 PM ET and lifted at 8:15 PM ET (weather.com puts the official end at ~8:19 PM ET); FlightAware's Friday-final tally was 9,159 cancellations and 7,190 delays on U.S. flights (AP), with 3,500+ aircraft airborne when it began; Saturday recovery added 2,500-3,500+ more cancellations. Cause, updated: new technology added to the ATC system overloaded antiquated equipment, causing intermittent communications and radar gaps; no evidence of a cyberattack -- contradicting inventoried O38's "major attack" framing. The post's own figures (6.6K+ cancelled, 8.6K delayed, "longest stop since 9/11") were mid-event counts. The caption is truncated in the UI at its most specific claims; the visualization itself was not viewable (black frame).
engine_training_value: The strongest in the selected 20: ADS-B tracks are labelled, timestamped movement data -- per-airport accumulation counts and charter-aircraft delay durations during a disruption are exactly a situational feature family (team travel disruption) with labels that exist in the public feed itself. This post supplies no dataset, but it identifies where the data lives (public ADS-B) and demonstrates the join.
